content: Professor Graham Brown, an Emeritus Professor at the University of Melbourne, Australia, has contributed significantly to the field of tropical medicine. Professor Tom Burkot, a Professor and Tropical Leader at the Australian Institute for Tropical Health and Medicine, James Cook University, Cairns, Australia, is recognized for his expertise in vector-borne diseases. Dr. Gabriel Carrasquilla, the Director of ASIESALUD, specializes in consultancy and research in epidemiology and public health. Professor Maureen Coetzee, a Professor and Director at the Wits Research Institute for Malaria, University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa, is a leading expert in malaria research. Professor Umberto d’Alessandro, the Director of the Medical Research Council Unit in Gambia, has made substantial contributions to malaria control strategies. Professor Abdoulaye Djimde, Head of the Molecular Epidemiology and Drug Resistance Unit at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Mali, Mali, is renowned for his work on antimalarial drug resistance. Professor Gao Qi, a Senior Professor at the Jiangsu Institute of Parasitic Diseases, Wuxi, China, is a distinguished researcher in parasitology. Professor Azra Ghani, Chair in Infectious Disease Epidemiology at the Faculty of Medicine, School of Public Health, Imperial College London, United Kingdom, is a leading figure in modeling the epidemiology of infectious diseases. Dr. Caroline Jones, a Senior Social Scientist at the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Kenya, has conducted extensive qualitative research on healthcare utilization in the context of malaria vaccine introduction. Dr. S.H. Chan, affiliated with the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, USA, has contributed to research on allele-specific immunity related to malaria vaccines. Professor Rakesh Aggarwal, Director of the Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), India, is a prominent figure in medical education and research. Professor Alejandro Cravioto, a Professor at the Facultad de Medicina, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, Mexico, serves as the Chair of SAGE (Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization). Dr. Ilesh Jani, Director General of the National Institute of Health, Ministry of Health, Mozambique, has played a pivotal role in public health initiatives. Dr. Jaleela Jawad, Head of the Immunization Group at the Public Health Directorate, Ministry of Health, Bahrain, is an expert in immunization programs. Dr. Sonali Kochhar, a Clinical Associate Professor in the Department of Global Health at the University of Washington, USA, has contributed to vaccine safety and global health research. Professor Noni MacDonald, a Professor of Pediatrics in the Division of Pediatric Infectious Diseases at Dalhousie University, Canada, is a leader in pediatric infectious disease research. Professor Shabir Madhi, a Professor of Vaccinology at the University of the Witwatersrand, South Africa, is a key figure in vaccine development and implementation. Professor Peter McIntyre, a Professor in the Department of Women’s and Children’s Health at the Dunedin School of Medicine, University of Otago, New Zealand, has contributed to maternal and child health research. Dr. Ezzeddine Mohsni, a Senior Technical Adviser at the Global Health Development (GHD) and the Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (EMPHNET), Jordan, is an expert in public health systems. Professor Kim Mulholland, affiliated with the Murdoch Children’s Research Institute, University of Melbourne, Australia, has made significant contributions to child health and immunization. Professor Kathleen Neuzil, Director of the Center for Vaccine Development and Global Health at the University of Maryland School of Medicine, USA, is a leading expert in vaccine research and development. Dr. Hanna Nohynek, Chief Physician at the Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL), Finland, has expertise in vaccine policy and implementation. Dr. Folake Olayinka, USAID Immunization Team Lead, USA, has been instrumental in advancing immunization programs globally. Professor Punnee Pitisuttithum, Head of the Department of Clinical Tropical Medicine at Mahidol University, Thailand, is a renowned expert in tropical medicine and vaccine trials. Professor Andrew J. from Zimbabwe and Professor Peter Smith from the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, United Kingdom, have contributed extensively to global health and infectious disease research. Professor S. Patrick Kachur, affiliated with the Mailman School of Public Health, Columbia University, USA, is a recognized expert in malaria control and prevention. Dr. Pedro Alonso, Director of the Global Malaria Programme, and Dr. Tracey Goodman, from the Expanded Programme on Immunization, have played key roles in advancing malaria vaccine implementation. Mr. John Grove, responsible for Quality Assurance, Norms, and Standards, and Dr. Joachim Hombach, involved in Agenda, Policy, and Strategy, have contributed to the development of WHO guidelines. Dr. Melanie Marti and Dr. Kate O’Brien, experts in Immunization, Vaccines, and Biologicals, have supported evidence-based recommendations for malaria vaccine deployment. Dr. Vaseeharan Sathiyamoorthy, specializing in Research for Health, and Ms. Cynthia Bergstrom, a consultant for WHO, have facilitated the transparent formulation of evidence-informed recommendations. Dr. Madhava Ram Balakrishnan and Dr. Shalini Desai, from the Expanded Programme on Immunization, have contributed to the systematic review of evidence. Dr. Mary Hamel and Dr. Dianliang Lei have provided expertise in immunization and biological standards. The systematic review team, including Gemma Villanueva and Nicholas Henschke from the Cochrane Response, supported the development of malaria vaccine recommendations by applying the PICO framework and GRADE methodology. Dr. Laurence Slutsker consolidated the evidence review for the SAGE/MPAG Working Group, ensuring a transparent link between evidence and recommendations. All SAGE and MPAG members updated their Declarations of Interest before the meeting, which were assessed by the WHO Secretariat. Relevant interests were disclosed, and members with potential conflicts recused themselves from decision-making during the malaria vaccine session. The full summary of interests is available on the WHO Malaria Vaccine Implementation Programme website. The third edition of the WHO Guidelines for the Treatment of Malaria was developed using updated WHO standard methods, ensuring a transparent link between evidence and recommendations. The process involved systematic reviews, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analyses, and extensive consultations with experts. Recommendations were agreed upon by consensus, supported by robust evidence, and reviewed by external experts to ensure accuracy and relevance.
